STAGE 1 — orientation
GOAL: find repo context and available tooling before drafting the idea.
READ: search("append_progress") -> tools.progress.append_progress exists; glob("**/*.py") in the agent workdir -> no files (empty sandbox).
OBSERVED: workdir is empty; only progress writes are permitted; no shell/read of the parent repo guaranteed.
REASONING: I must ground the proposal in the stated objective and the CURVCTRL-SID defect (saturated curvature cap) rather than in unseen code. The defect lesson: any behaviour-derived scalar that a protective bound saturates makes the behaviour term non-load-bearing. So the new mechanism must either (a) use the normalised-input exp_0^c rule where the ball constraint holds for all c, or (b) use a behaviour statistic that enters as a *ratio/normalised quantity* by construction.
OPEN: confirm which geometric carrier and which behaviour statistic to couple.

STAGE 2 — design lock
GOAL: pick a coupling position not used by the rejected rounds (cocond-markov-poincare-ot / poincare-frechet-successor-codebook / CURVCTRL-SID / LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE / behcone-prefix / succboost-geoshift), and immune to the CURVCTRL defect.
READ: the defect note — CURVCTRL derived c_l=(1/Q_l-1)/rho_l^2 then capped at 0.99/max|z|^2, and the cap bound for every Q<0.95, so the behaviour statistic was constant after the clamp.
OBSERVED: the load-bearing quantity must never be truncated by a protective bound; the safest construction is a monotone map onto a MEASURED image, not a clamp.
REASONING: chosen position = behaviour sets the RADIAL coordinate of a curved assignment probe (capacity matching), fixed curvature c=1, so behaviour lives in r_l and geometry in exp_0^c / d_c. No clamp exists: the map's image is [0.07,1.0]xR_ref by construction, listed explicitly. Distinct from all six prior ideas, which put behaviour into mass (Sinkhorn), into codebook means (Frechet), into curvature (CURVCTRL), into smoothing (Lorentz), into cones, or into a shift.
OPEN: none; writing the final block.

STAGE 3 — final answer produced (condensed record; full text is in the chat reply)
IDEA: RADCAP-SID. Behaviour = per-level branchiness of training transitions, H_l = mean entropy of the next level-l SID prefix given the current one (nats), N_l = exp(H_l); geometry = FIXED curvature c=1, Poincare exp_0^c and distance d_c. Coupling = behaviour sets the RADIAL coordinate of the assignment probe: r_l = R_ref * log1p(N_l)/log1p(24556), R_ref = measured 0.9-quantile of training ||z||; probe = exp_0^c(r_l * z/||z||); k* = argmin_k d_c(probe, e_k^l); commitment = d_c(z, e_k)^2; RQ residual and decoder unchanged.
WHY IT IS SAFE AGAINST THE CURVCTRL DEFECT: no clamp on the behaviour term at all. The map's image is [0.069,1.0]xR_ref (14x working range) and R_ref is a measured 0.90 quantile, so r_l sits in roughly [0.04,0.45] inside a ball of radius 1. The domain guards (1-c||.||^2, arcosh arg) are logged and expected to fire zero times.
WHY IT IS DISTINCT: prior rounds put behaviour into codebook means (Frechet), assignment mass (Sinkhorn/OT), the curvature itself (CURVCTRL), neighbour smoothing (Lorentz profile), a cone constraint (behcone) or a post-hoc shift (succboost). RADCAP leaves codebook, residual chain and reconstruction untouched and modulates only the radius, i.e. the capacity coordinate of the level.
COST at frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps, L=4, K=256, d=32, B=1024): 1.05M curved pair evaluations per step, ~0.3-0.5 GFLOP extra vs ~0.03 GFLOP plain L2 => +8-15% step time, +1.5-3 h; per-epoch H_l/R_ref recount 1-2 s => +1-1.7 h over the run. No new parameters.
ABLATIONS EXIST BUT UNTRAINED: behaviour-off = H_l replaced by pooled constant H_ref across levels; geometry-off = c->0 (probe = Euclidean rescale, L2 distance and L2 commitment), r_l unchanged; both-on = the full mechanism.
JUDGEMENT: stage-3 test recall@10 vs 0.065 in one run, with per-level entropy/hit-rate/used-code-count logged as diagnostics only.
OPEN: none.

STAGE RECORD 1 (ideation, single idea, round after CURVCTRL-SID defect)
GOAL: choose a coupling position that is materially different from the four already-measured positions (Sinkhorn successor cost = cocond-markov-poincare-ot; successor-weighted Frechet codebook update = poincare-frechet-successor-codebook; per-level curvature from hard prefix hit rate = CURVCTRL-SID; successor cone / boost-shift / Lorentz profile / mixed-curvature fibre variants).
WHAT I READ / USED: the defect report description in the prompt (cap c_l <= 0.99/max|z|^2 bound for every Q_l below ~0.95, so the applied curvature was constant) and the endorsed amendment (normalise the input first, z_hat = z/max|z|, then map with exp_0^c, so the ball constraint holds for ANY c and the behaviour statistic stays load-bearing over its whole range).
OBSERVED: the failure mode is a protective cap on the CURVATURE that saturates the behaviour statistic. Any new mechanism must either avoid capping the behaviour-driven quantity at all, or show the operating range explicitly.
REASONING: instead of putting behaviour into the curvature (saturated by a ball constraint) or into the codebook update (already done), put behaviour into the RADIAL COORDINATE of a fixed-curvature Poincare point, and put geometry into the quantizer's nearest-codeword score. Then the ball constraint is satisfied structurally (normalise the direction, take the radius from a rank map bounded by 0.9 < 1) and there is no cap on the behaviour stat at all; the curvature c = 1 is derived from the direction normalisation, not tuned.
ANSWER CHOICE: single idea "BRad-RQ" (behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment for the RQ-VAE quantizer). Distinct from all prior positions: no Sinkhorn, no Frechet codebook update, no per-level curvature, no cone, no translation/boost, no successor cost term.
STILL OPEN: numeric range check (done in record 2) and full 20-field answer block (record 4).

STAGE RECORD 4 (final answer summary; full block printed in the reply because one record is capped at 4000 chars). IDEA: BRad-RQ - Behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment for the RQ-VAE quantizer. Coupling position differs from all four measured positions (Sinkhorn successor cost, successor-weighted Frechet codebook update, per-level curvature from prefix hit rate, cone/boost/Lorentz/fibre variants): behaviour sets the RADIAL COORDINATE only, curvature is fixed at c=1 and hence can never be saturated. Behaviour signal: exp(H_i), the effective number of distinct predecessor contexts, from directed consecutive-item counts C[j,i] over training sequences, entropy H_i over p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i, shrunk to sbar = mean{exp(H_i): n_i>=10} with weight 1/(n_i+1); unseen items get sbar. Radius: u_i = rank(s_i)/(N+1), rho_i = 0.9*u_i, r_i = artanh(rho_i), t_i = r_i * z_i/|z_i|, p_i = exp_0(t_i). Assignment: k_l = argmin_k |a-e_lk|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e_lk|^2)) with a = clamp(residual), e = exp_0(squash(m_lk)); residual updated Euclidean in the tangent frame; reconstruction/commitment stay Euclidean on t. NUMERIC RANGE CHECK (own record): rho in (0,0.9) -> r in (0,1.4722); 1-rho^2 >= 0.19; tanh(0.9)=0.7163 for codeword norms; behaviour-off r = artanh(0.45) = 0.4847; per-step 1024*3*256 = 786432 distance evals, ~1.6e8 flops, <2 percent of an epoch. Because the 0.9 margin is applied to the INPUT rank map before artanh (normalise-first rule), no protective bound truncates the behaviour statistic over its whole range, unlike CURVCTRL-SID. Switches: behaviour-off (rho_i = 0.45 constant), geometry-off (Euclidean score, identity exp), both-on. Judged by one frozen Stage3 run, target test_recall@10 > 0.065; prefix-radius correlation and level-1 prefix entropy are recorded only.
